title: Sub Rosa

description.main: Sub Rosa gathers a body of photographic collage by ceramic sculptor Ron Nagle, made by splicing photo-booth self-portraits into found postcards. Published for exhibitions at Fridericianum, Kassel, and Secession, Vienna, in 2019, with a text by Nagle and a conversation with Massimiliano Gioni.
description.extended:
Sub Rosa gathers a private practice of collage that runs alongside Ron Nagle's better-known career as a ceramic sculptor, revealing an artist who has spent decades merging vintage postcards with photo-booth self-portraits into small, uncanny tableaux.

Published on the occasion of two exhibitions — Euphoric Recall at Fridericianum, Kassel, and a solo show at Secession, Vienna, both in 2019 — the hardcover volume reproduces the collages alongside a text by Nagle and a conversation with curator Massimiliano Gioni. Nagle describes taking hundreds of photographs of himself at a novelty photo booth on San Francisco's 24th Street, then splicing the results into found postcards until a convincing tableau emerged, letting him, in his words, "insinuate myself into a scene from someone else's experience."

Nagle (b. 1939, San Francisco) began as a studio assistant to Peter Voulkos and became a central figure of the California Clay Movement, developing the small-scale, jewel-colored ceramic sculptures for which he is best known; he is represented by Matthew Marks Gallery. Sub Rosa documents the parallel, largely unseen collage practice running alongside that sculptural work.
description.artist_bio: Ron Nagle (b. 1939, San Francisco) began as a studio assistant to Peter Voulkos and became a central figure of the California Clay Movement, working small-scale, jewel-colored ceramic sculptures embellished with epoxy and synthetic materials. He is represented by Matthew Marks Gallery and Modern Art (London), and his work is held in major museum and private collections. He is also a musician and songwriter, formerly of the San Francisco band The Mystery Trend.
description.exhibition_context: Sub Rosa was published on the occasion of two exhibitions: Euphoric Recall at Fridericianum, Kassel (June 6 – September 8, 2019), and a solo exhibition at Secession, Vienna (November 23, 2019 – February 9, 2020).

notes: Two sources conflicted on pagination/dimensions: Fridericianum's own page listed 136 pp at 14.7 x 10.5 cm, while Idea Books, Amazon UK, KARMA Bookstore, and the basis wien archive record (citing '[60] Bl.' = 60 leaves = 120 pp) independently agree on 120 pp at 11 3/4 x 9 in. Went with the majority-sourced figure (120 pp / 11 3/4 x 9 in) as more likely correct; Fridericianum's figures may reflect a data-entry error on that page. Cover sourced from KARMA Bookstore (flat, front-on product shot); Fridericianum's own cover image was a 3/4-angle installation-style shot of the same edition, confirming the design matches.
